subject: Request: Temporary SLA carve-out for content-guard tool-call timeouts / structured-output failures
messages:
From: Ella Thompson <ella@medifin.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: samir@medifin.com, procurement@medifin.com
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected timeouts from content-guard chain impacting live payouts

Hi Vivek —

We're seeing intermittent 500s and long tail latency when our product calls Redwood for generation that triggers content-guard and then the structured-output post-processing. Between 03:40-08:50 PDT today, ~0.9% of calls either timed out waiting on the filter or returned malformed JSON from the structured-output step. That failure mode is blocking downstream payout generation in our platform and has resulted in a small number of delayed transactions.

Can your team confirm whether this is an outage on your side or a degradation introduced by the new third-party moderation adapter we enabled last week? We need to understand whether this impacts our SLA and whether we should expect credits or a temporary exemption while you remediate.

Links: I've attached a short capture and included our incident ticket.

Thanks,
Ella Thompson
Head of Integrations, MediFin Labs
E: ella@medifin.com
T: +1 415-555-0183

Attachments: medifin_incident_capture_0402.json
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Thompson <ella@medifin.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected timeouts from content-guard chain impacting live payouts

Hi Ella —

Sorry to see this. Thanks for the capture — Marcus pulled logs immediately. Preliminary take: during the 03:40–09:00 window we had elevated queue depth on the content-guard layer in us-west-2 tied to increased moderation adapter retries to a partner endpoint. That increased end-to-end p95 by ~180ms and caused a small number of request-level timeouts in customers with very tight upstream timeouts (looks like MediFin's payout worker uses a 700ms generation deadline).

Short answers:
- This was not an intentional config change on your account.
- Root cause appears to be partner adapter retries cascading into our filter tier under a specific payload pattern.
- We're throttling adapter retries and applying a quick filter-root backpressure fix now.

Immediate offer: We can provide a temporary carve-out for SLA attribution for content-guard-induced latency while we push the mitigation and run a patch. That would mean we do not apply uptime/latency credit triggers for filter/tool-call failures matching the incident fingerprints for the 48h remediation window.

Questions for you:
1) Do you accept a 48-hour attribution carve-out (starting at 03:40 PDT)?
2) Will you require a formal amendment/DocuSign to proceed, or is a short email confirmation sufficient for your procurement/legal team?

I'll loop in Neha to coordinate contractual language if you prefer an amendment.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
S: vivek@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_runtime_logs_20280401.zip (logs excerpt)
From: Ella Thompson <ella@medifin.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medifin.com, samir@medifin.com
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected timeouts from content-guard chain impacting live payouts

Vivek —

Appreciate the quick triage. A few notes from our side:
- We can accept a temporary attribution carve-out in principle, but procurement will want the language and dates documented for audit.
- We also need clarity on whether the carve-out covers structured-output parsing failures (malformed JSON) that your structured-output post-processor returned for ~0.2% of the affected calls. Those malformed payloads caused our parser to retry and double-charge a subset of wallet top-ups.

Next steps for us: procurement prefers a short amendment (1 page) that:
1) lists the incident fingerprint (time window + signature),
2) specifies the 48h carve-out period and its start time,
3) confirms that the carve-out is only for attribution (i.e., we retain rights to request quality remediation/fees if there is negligence), and
4) provides contact for RCA and post-mortem.

If you can get a draft over by tomorrow EOD we can fast-track.

Thanks,
Ella

Attachment: incident_ticket_#MDF-8472

Subject: Draft: 1-page amendment for MDR-DF-78321 (temporary attribution carve-out)

Hi Ella / Procurement —

Attached is a short draft amendment that captures the carve-out terms you requested. High-level summary:
- Scope: Attribution exclusion for content-guard and structured-output failures matching the attached fingerprints between 2028-04-02T03:40:00Z and 2028-04-04T03:40:00Z.
- Duration: 48 hours from the documented start time.
- Effect: Temporary attribution only; does not waive Redwood's responsibility to remediate or preclude remediation-based credits if issues persist beyond the window.
- RCA commitment: Full post-mortem within 5 business days and a technical remediation plan.

Please review and let us know any edits. If procurement confirms approval, we'll route the amendment for DocuSign.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor

neha@redwood.ai
